newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian defence minister sees no threat from NATO.
newsitem.headline: Russian defence minister sees no threat from NATO.

text.p: Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov said on Tuesday he was convinced NATO no longer posed a threat to the coungtry's security.

Rodionov was asked by reporters if talks with visiting British Defence Minister Michael Portillo had persuaded him there was no threat. "I am convinced but now I have to convince millions of people, above all in Russia, and we have to work on this. Just as we have to convince the West that Russia poses no threat to the West," Rodionov said.

Speaking after talks with Portillo following his arrival on a two-day visit to Moscow, Rodionov said some countries west of Russia -- including former East Bloc countries who are seeking NATO membership -- were still afraid of Moscow.
"Unfortunately many people to the west of Russia are still afraid. This is a natural process," he said.
Russia has vigorously opposed NATO plans to expand to the east, but has recently softened its stance in a tacit recognition that it can do little to stop the expansion.
Portillo said all sides must work to convince people that the end of the Cold War had removed a mutual threat. "We must each work on our public attitudes at home," said Portillo.
